english.title: Football spectator making false statement for exemption - banning order
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) in connection with an application under Section 20 of the Football Spectators Act 1989 for exemption from the requirements imposed by or under the Act, at or in respect of any regulated football match to which the application relates, made a statement which you knew to be false or misleading in a material particular or recklessly made a statement which was false or misleading in a material particular in that **(..SPECIFY statement..)
english.legislation: Contrary to section 20(10)(a) and (11) of the Football Spectators Act 1989.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
makes a statement which you knew to be false / misleading in a material particular or
recklessly makes a statement which is false / misleading in a material particular

investigatoraction.description: Guilty Plea by letter procedure may be offered for this offence
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) This wording differs from H4270. It introduces amendments made by the Football (Disorder) Act 2000 which combined Domestic and International Football Banning Orders as Banning Orders.
(ii) H4270 will remain valid until the end of the expiry period for International Football Banning Orders introduced under the Football (Offences and Disorder) Act 1999 which is 26 September 2004.
(iii) See the Football Spectators (Prescription) Order 2000, SI 2126/2000 for a definition of a "regulated" football match which covers certain association football matches and international matches.
(iv) Now PNC recordable from 18/08/07 as per S.I. 2007/2121
